editor_note: All four rewritten headings keep the English meaning and read naturally: "Cell ng paunawa sa setup", "Cell ng mga paunang kinakailangan", "Muling pagsulat ng path ng larawan" and "Pinagmulang code" (a defensible choice for "source code").

Nothing here would mislead a learner. The card descriptions keep their meaning, including the caveat about extra sampling overhead in [12], the PEC overhead reduction in [16] and the M3 subspace idea in [26]. In [4], "build on Qiskit's performant foundation" became "nagtitiwala sa matibay na pundasyon", which means "trust in the sturdy foundation". That is the wrong verb, and "performant" was turned into "sturdy". The card link text "Browse documentation" is handled three ways across the page: left in English, "I-browse ang dokumentasyon" in [7], and "Tingnan ang dokumentasyon" in [16] and [19]. "Backpropagating" in [12] became the awkward coinage "pagbabalik-propagasyon", and "learning noise models" in [15] became "pag-aaral" ("studying"), which misses the sense of characterizing a model from data.

examples.source: These modular software components build on Qiskit's performant foundation
examples.translation: nagtitiwala sa matibay na pundasyon ng Qiskit
examples.suggested: nakabatay sa mabilis at mahusay na pundasyon ng Qiskit
examples.why: 'nagtitiwala' means 'trusts/relies on', not 'builds on', and 'matibay' (sturdy) is not the same as 'performant'.

examples.source: linkText="Browse documentation"
examples.translation: Tingnan ang dokumentasyon (vs. 'I-browse ang dokumentasyon' in [7] and English kept elsewhere)
examples.suggested: Use one rendering, e.g. 'Tingnan ang dokumentasyon', on every card
examples.why: The same UI label is rendered three different ways on one page.

examples.source: by backpropagating observables through the circuit
examples.translation: sa pamamagitan ng pagbabalik-propagasyon ng mga observable sa buong circuit
examples.suggested: sa pamamagitan ng pag-backpropagate ng mga observable sa circuit
examples.why: 'pagbabalik-propagasyon' is a stiff coinage; the field keeps 'backpropagate' as a loanword, which matches the card title.

examples.source: tools for learning and refining noise models
examples.translation: para sa pag-aaral at pagpino ng mga noise model
examples.suggested: para sa pag-learn (pagtukoy) at pagpino ng mga noise model
examples.why: 'pag-aaral' reads as a human studying the models, not as inferring or characterizing them from experimental data.

editor_note: None of the five rewritten headings would mislead a learner. There are two small consistency issues. First, entry 2 uses the Tagalog "kalibrasyon", but everywhere else the page keeps "calibration": the frontmatter title (entry 1, "Monitoring, mga calibration, at benchmarking"), the "Calibrating" heading, and all of the body text. So the H1 no longer matches its own page title. Second, entries 37 and 41 ("Performance ng single-qubit", "Performance ng two-qubit") use "single-qubit" as if it were a noun. The sibling headings in entries 17 and 22 use the adjectival "Mga single-qubit na operasyon", so the parallel form is "Single-qubit na performance". "Pagmomonitor ng parameter" (6) and "Holistikong pagmomonitor" (13) are natural and faithful.

examples.source: Monitoring, calibrations, and benchmarking
examples.translation: Pagmomonitor, kalibrasyon, at benchmarking
examples.suggested: Pagmomonitor, mga calibration, at benchmarking
examples.why: The rest of the file, including the page title in entry 1, uses 'calibration'. 'kalibrasyon' appears only here, so the H1 is inconsistent with the title and the body.

examples.source: Single-qubit performance
examples.translation: Performance ng single-qubit
examples.suggested: Single-qubit na performance
examples.why: This treats the compound modifier as a noun ('performance of single-qubit'). The sibling headings in entries 17 and 22 use the adjectival 'single-qubit na …' pattern. The same fix applies to entry 41 ('Two-qubit na performance').

editor_note: The translation is faithful and natural, and the caveats are all kept, for example "kasalukuyang nasa beta at nangangailangan ng `qiskit-ibm-runtime` bersyon 0.47.0 o mas mataas" and "Nailabas na ... mula pa sa v0.45.0".

The meaning is faithful all the way through. The caveats come through intact: the account won't activate without the final step, not to enter credit card details unless upgrading, the email must not already be tied to an IBM Cloud account, and students can't see other instances' data. The 10-minute / 28-day quota and the physics-101-john-doe prefix example also match the English. Two small wording slips: "Direktahin" in the Recommendations tip [41] is an awkward coinage where "Ituro"/"Idirekta" would read naturally, and [14] says the same thing twice ("hindi kasalukuyang nakakabit sa isang umiiral na").

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The caveats (no simulator yet, Sampler-only scope, shots apply to the whole job, twirling must be undone manually with XOR) are all kept, so nothing would mislead a learner. The problems are wording. "Settings live" is calqued as "naninirahan" (entry 71), "behavior" becomes "ugali" (entry 13), and "sampol" is used as a bare verb in entry 12, which also calques "expected to arrive soon" as "darating na malapit". Step headings are inconsistent: "Hakbang 1–6" but "Step 7" and "Step 8" (entries 86 and 92). Entry 57 uses the completed-aspect verb "idineklara mo" where a general instruction needs "idinedeklara mo".

examples.translation: May pagkakaiba rin sa istruktura kung saan naninirahan ang mga setting.
examples.suggested: May pagkakaiba rin sa istruktura kung saan itinatakda ang mga setting.
examples.why: 'Naninirahan' means to reside or dwell, as a person does. It is a literal calque of the English idiom 'live' and reads oddly for configuration settings.

examples.source: Step 7. Change how you access results

examples.suggested: Hakbang 7. Baguhin kung paano mo ina-access ang mga resulta

examples.source: Reproducing Estimator's behavior with Executor
examples.translation: Ang pag-reproduce ng ugali ng Estimator gamit ang Executor
examples.suggested: Ang paggaya sa gawi ng Estimator gamit ang Executor

None of the 7 rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 20 keeps the non-commutation argument intact (ZZII vs YYYY on qubit 3, the uncertainty relation, and the 16x16 matrix being easy to diagonalize), and entry 21 is faithful. The problems are consistency and wording. Heading 53 switches to "Klasikal na Workflow" when the parent heading (51) and the rest of the page use "classical workflow". Headings 141 and 145 translate the method names ("Quantum Diagonalization na Batay sa Sampling", "Configuration Interaction ng Quantum Subspace"), but the body text right under them and the sibling KQD heading keep the English names. editor_note: The rewritten heading [29] "Function ng Loss" is only half translated. It flips the English compound into a Tagalog possessive, which reads like "function of the Loss", and capitalizes "Loss" as if it were a proper noun. It also doesn't match the rest of the page, where the body keeps the term as "loss function" throughout ([30], [31], [63], [83]). A learner would still recognize the concept, so it is not misleading, but a native editor would change the heading to "Loss function" to match the body.

examples.source: Loss function {#loss-function}
examples.translation: Function ng Loss {#loss-function}
examples.suggested: Loss function {#loss-function}
examples.why: This half-translated possessive calque reads as 'function of the Loss', and 'Loss' is wrongly capitalized. It doesn't match the body, which keeps the term as 'loss function' in [30], [31], [63] and [83]. The heading should use the same term as the body.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The facts all match the English: the T1/T2 discussion, the coherent-vs-incoherent accumulation, the p→1 dephasing subtlety, the rule that Z errors on the target can't reach the control through ZZ while X/Y can, and the CNOT error-propagation table. Terms are split between the two halves of the page. The first half keeps "state", "probability" and "noise" in English, while from about [184] on it switches to "estado", "posibilidad" and "ingay" (and the heading at [10] already says "Ingay na thermal"). There are also a few calques and garbled clauses: "i-calibrate palayo" (calibrated away), "ang order ng libu-libong two-qubit gates", "Ang mga diagonal term ay ang kabuuan ay 1", and in [292] a passive "hindi maaapektuhan" where an active verb is needed.

examples.source: An error at the same layer as the measurement, but on a different qubit, cannot affect the measurement
examples.translation: Ang isang error sa parehong layer kung saan may measurement, pero sa ibang qubit, ay hindi maaapektuhan ang measurement
examples.suggested: ...ay hindi makakaapekto sa measurement
examples.why: The passive 'hindi maaapektuhan' is ungrammatical here and could be read as the error being the thing that is unaffected. It needs the active 'makakaapekto sa'.

examples.source: the probability of measuring $|0\rangle$ state to increase
examples.translation: tataas ang posibilidad ng pagsukat sa estadong $|0\rangle$
examples.suggested: tataas ang probability na masukat ang state na $|0\rangle$ (match the first half), or use one rendering throughout
examples.why: The first half uses 'probability' and 'state' (e.g. [98], [129]), but from about [184] on the page switches to 'posibilidad' and 'estado'. Likewise 'noise' becomes 'ingay'. Each concept should have one rendering throughout the file.

examples.source: But they can be partially calibrated away
examples.translation: Ngunit maaari itong bahagyang i-calibrate palayo
examples.suggested: Ngunit maaari itong bahagyang maalis sa pamamagitan ng calibration
examples.why: 'i-calibrate palayo' copies the English phrasal verb word for word and doesn't read like Tagalog. The same calque appears in [107].

examples.source: we might plausibly implement on the order of thousands of two-qubit gates
examples.translation: maaari nating maipatupad ang order ng libu-libong two-qubit gates
examples.suggested: maaari nating maipatupad ang humigit-kumulang libu-libong two-qubit gates
examples.why: 'ang order ng' is a stiff calque of 'on the order of'. A native writer would say 'humigit-kumulang' or 'nasa libu-libo'.

examples.source: We used only 100 shots here, which is unusually low
examples.translation: na hindi karaniwang mababa
examples.suggested: na di-pangkaraniwang mababa
examples.why: 'hindi karaniwang mababa' can be read as 'not usually low', which is the opposite of the intended 'unusually low'. 'di-pangkaraniwang' removes the ambiguity.

editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries changes the meaning, but a native editor would still fix a few things. Entry 28 reads like machine translation. "Magiging magaling kung" is a calque of "it would be great" ("magaling" means skilled). "Anuman ang opsyon ang totoo" and "Maisip mo ba ng isang eksperimento" are ungrammatical. It also says "mga opsyon ng Einstein at Born" where entry 29 correctly uses "nina". In entry 32, "ibang particle" means "a different particle" rather than "the other particle" ("kabilang particle"). The heading in entry 136 uses "pang-unawa" while entries 27 and 110 use "pag-unawa".

examples.source: It would be great to distinguish between the Einstein and Born options experimentally.
examples.translation: Magiging magaling kung matukoy natin ang pagkakaiba sa pagitan ng mga opsyon ng Einstein at Born sa pamamagitan ng eksperimento.
examples.suggested: Maganda sana kung matutukoy natin sa eksperimento ang pagkakaiba ng mga opsyon nina Einstein at Born.
examples.why: 'Magaling' means skilled, so this is a calque of 'it would be great'. Personal names also need 'nina', as entry 29 has it.

examples.source: ...regardless of which option is true? Can you think of an experiment that would yield different results for the two options?
examples.translation: ...anuman ang opsyon ang totoo? Maisip mo ba ng isang eksperimento na magbibigay ng iba't ibang mga resulta para sa dalawang opsyon?
examples.suggested: ...alinmang opsyon ang totoo? May maiisip ka bang eksperimento na magbibigay ng magkaibang resulta para sa dalawang opsyon?
examples.why: Both clauses are ungrammatical: 'anuman ... ang totoo' and 'Maisip mo ba ng'.

examples.source: a measurement of the other particle along the $y$ axis must also yield $+y$
examples.translation: ang pagsukat ng ibang particle sa $y$ axis ay dapat ding magbigay ng $+y$
examples.suggested: ang pagsukat sa kabilang particle sa $y$ axis ay dapat ding magbigay ng $+y$
examples.why: 'Ibang' means 'a different' particle. 'Kabilang' is the paired 'other'.

examples.source: Check your understanding
examples.translation: Suriin ang iyong pang-unawa
examples.suggested: Suriin ang iyong pag-unawa
examples.why: The same heading is 'pag-unawa' in entries 27 and 110, so this one should match.

editor_note: None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 9 (video title) and entry 47 (the reversed-order measurement explanation, including the collapse into an x eigenstate and "mas masahol pa dito") keep the English meaning intact. Two phrasings are still stiff enough that a native editor would fix them. In entry 66, "tama ito nang tinatayang" is a word-for-word calque of "approximately correct" and should read "tinatayang tama ito". In entry 47, the last sentence "gaano katiyak o kawalang-katiyakan" pairs an adjective with a noun, so "gaano katiyak o hindi katiyak" would be the natural parallel form.

examples.source: Indeed this approximately correct for the state we chose.
examples.translation: Sa katunayan, tama ito nang tinatayang para sa estadong pinili natin.
examples.suggested: Sa katunayan, tinatayang tama ito para sa estadong pinili natin.
examples.why: 'tama ito nang tinatayang' copies the English adverb order and reads as awkward, near-ungrammatical Tagalog. The adverb belongs before the adjective.

examples.source: Let's investigate how certain or uncertain a quantity is for a given state.
examples.translation: Tuklasin natin kung gaano katiyak o kawalang-katiyakan ang isang dami para sa isang naibigay na estado.
examples.suggested: Suriin natin kung gaano katiyak o hindi katiyak ang isang dami para sa isang partikular na estado.
examples.why: 'katiyak' (adjective) is paired with 'kawalang-katiyakan' (noun), so the 'gaano ...' construction is broken. 'naibigay na' is a calque of 'given'.

editor_note: Entry 22's heading "1b: Mga Multi-Product Formula" is faithful and idiomatic: it marks the plural with "Mga" and keeps the English term in the singular, which matches "Mga MPF" and "mga product formula" elsewhere on the page.

Five of the six rewritten entries are fine: the headings "Pangkalahatang-ideya ng Noise Learning/Post-processing" and "Mga resource sa antas ng laptop/cluster", and the list item "Suporta sa Qiskit Visualization". The one issue is in the table in entry 22. "Repeat identity pairs of layers" became "Ulitin ang mga magkapares na identity layer" ("paired identity layers"), which suggests each layer is an identity layer. In the English, it is the pair of layers (a layer and its inverse) that makes the identity. The table's images and the surrounding text make the intent recoverable, so this does not rise to a misleading FAIL, but it should be reworded.

examples.source: Repeat identity pairs of layers and learn noise
examples.translation: Ulitin ang mga magkapares na identity layer at alamin ang noise
examples.suggested: Ulitin ang mga pares ng layer na bumubuo ng identity at alamin ang noise
examples.why: 'magkapares na identity layer' says the layers themselves are identity layers. In the source, the layer and its inverse together form the identity. This is a small but real change of meaning in a step that teaches how noise is learned.

editor_note: The rewritten entry 11, "Self-consistent na loop ng pagbawi ng configuration", keeps the meaning and does not mislead. The problem is consistency: it translates "recovery" as "pagbawi", while entries 2, 19 and 21 keep the named technique in English as "configuration recovery technique" and "self-consistent configuration recovery". That splits one named method across two forms. Using "Self-consistent na configuration recovery loop" would make this step-4 heading match the rest of the page.

examples.source: Self-consistent configuration recovery loop
examples.translation: Self-consistent na loop ng pagbawi ng configuration
examples.suggested: Self-consistent na configuration recovery loop
examples.why: Everywhere else on the page (entries 2, 19, 21) the named technique stays in English as 'configuration recovery'. Translating it only here as 'pagbawi ng configuration' makes it harder for the learner to link this step to the technique described in the intro and diagram text.

editor_note: Entry 11 keeps the English meaning, so a learner won't be misled. The problem is that it translates the named technique "configuration recovery" as "pagbawi ng configuration", while the rest of the page keeps the English term ("configuration recovery technique" in [2], "enhanced configuration recovery" in [33]). Because of that, the step heading no longer matches the named SQD technique used elsewhere on the page. Keep the English term here too, so the heading reads "Self-consistent na configuration recovery loop".

examples.source: Self-consistent configuration recovery loop
examples.translation: Self-consistent na loop ng pagbawi ng configuration
examples.suggested: Self-consistent na configuration recovery loop
examples.why: The page keeps 'configuration recovery' in English as the name of the technique ([2], [33]). Translating it only here breaks the link between this step and that technique. The meaning is still correct, so this is a minor consistency issue.

editor_note: Entry 0 is a faithful, natural Tagalog rendering. "Ipinapakita ng tutorial na ito kung paano isakatuparan ang isang Nishimori phase transition" keeps "demonstrates" and "realize" accurate, and it keeps the term "Nishimori phase transition" consistent with the heading in entry 1.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The results discussion ([148]-[151]) keeps its numbers and its caveat that the 10% bias band applies only to PEC+SLC. The biggest slip is in [135], where "ranks the errors" became "itinutugma" ("matches"), which blurs the ranking step (in [29] "Rank" is rendered "Ranggo"). The heading [134] was left in English, and step headings switch between "Hakbang" and "Step" ("Step 2: Optimize" and "Step 1/3/4" in the body). There are also some awkward phrasings: "circuit na interesado" in [30], "Ikintal" for "insert", and bare "ay commute sa" in [90]/[91]/[98].

examples.source: It then ranks the errors by how worthwhile they are to mitigate
examples.translation: Pagkatapos, itinutugma nito ang mga error base sa kung gaano kabuti ang mitigation sa mga ito
examples.suggested: Pagkatapos, niraranggo nito ang mga error ayon sa kung gaano kasulit na i-mitigate ang mga ito
examples.why: 'itinutugma' means 'matches', not 'ranks'. The sorting/prioritization step is lost, though the next clause still says a subset is selected.

examples.source: b.ii. Compute the `local_scales` for the hardware execution
examples.translation: b.ii. Compute the `local_scales` for the hardware execution
examples.suggested: b.ii. Kalkulahin ang `local_scales` para sa hardware execution
examples.why: Heading left untranslated, while all the sibling headings are translated.

examples.source: Insert anti-noise and run. Execute the circuit of interest with anti-noise
examples.translation: Ikintal ang anti-noise at patakbuhin. Isagawa ang circuit na interesado gamit ang anti-noise
examples.suggested: Ilagay ang anti-noise at patakbuhin. Isagawa ang target na circuit gamit ang anti-noise
examples.why: 'circuit na interesado' says the circuit itself is interested (a calque). 'Ikintal' (to imprint/instill) is an odd choice for 'insert'.

examples.source: Step 2: Optimize
examples.translation: Step 2: Optimize
examples.suggested: Hakbang 2: I-optimize
examples.why: Inconsistent with 'Hakbang 1/3/4' in the other headings; body text also uses 'Step 1', 'Step 3', 'Step 4'.

examples.source: the X measurement on qubit 6 commutes with the X error
examples.translation: ang X measurement sa qubit 6 ay commute sa X error
examples.suggested: ang X measurement sa qubit 6 ay nagko-commute sa X error
examples.why: Bare English verb without Tagalog affix. [110] uses the natural 'nagko-commute', so usage within the file is inconsistent.

editor_note: I found nothing that would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful throughout, including the geometric-separation and model-complexity conditions in [58] and the ZNE and 80-minute caveats. The problems are register and phrasing. The reader is addressed inconsistently: the plural or polite "ninyo/inyong" in [30] and [52] against "mo/iyong/ikaw" elsewhere, with [52] mixing both in one paragraph. "Training" is kept as "training" in [46] but becomes "pagsasanay" in [52]. There are also a few calques: "binubuksan" (literally "opening") for turning on error mitigation, "Inilalabas" for "print out", and the clumsy "mas maliit nang malaki kaysa sa $N$".

examples.source: Note that we turn on error mitigation, including Zero Noise Extrapolation (ZNE).
examples.translation: Tandaan na binubuksan natin ang error mitigation, kasama ang Zero Noise Extrapolation (ZNE).
examples.suggested: Tandaan na pinapagana natin ang error mitigation, kasama ang Zero Noise Extrapolation (ZNE).
examples.why: "Binubuksan" literally means opening, which is a calque of "turn on". For enabling a setting, "pinapagana" or "ina-activate" is the natural word.

examples.source: ...included in the files you downloaded... If you performed the training yourself, you can continue the tutorial with your own results.
examples.translation: ...na kasama sa mga file na na-download ninyo... Kung ikaw ay nagsagawa ng pagsasanay sa iyong sarili, maaari kang magpatuloy...
examples.suggested: ...na kasama sa mga file na na-download mo... Kung ikaw mismo ang nagpatakbo ng training, maaari kang magpatuloy sa tutorial gamit ang sarili mong mga resulta.
examples.why: One paragraph switches between the plural or polite "ninyo" and the singular "ikaw". It also renders "training" as "pagsasanay", while [46] keeps it as "training".

examples.source: You can run this tutorial by running the following cell...
examples.translation: Maaari ninyong patakbuhin ang tutorial na ito...sa inyong environment. Kung mayroon na kayong mga file...
examples.suggested: Maaari mong patakbuhin ang tutorial na ito...sa iyong environment. Kung mayroon ka nang mga file...
examples.why: This entry addresses the reader with the plural or polite "ninyo/kayo". Most of the file uses the casual singular "mo/ka", which the informal-register convention expects.

examples.source: while the quantum-projected model complexity is substantially smaller than $N$
examples.translation: habang ang quantum-projected na model complexity ay mas maliit nang malaki kaysa sa $N$
examples.suggested: habang ang quantum-projected na model complexity ay mas maliit nang husto kaysa sa $N$
examples.why: "Mas maliit nang malaki" (literally "smaller by a large amount") is a clumsy, self-contradictory-sounding calque. "Mas maliit nang husto" or "lubhang mas maliit" reads naturally.

examples.source: We print out the circuit size and the two-qubit gate depth.
examples.translation: Inilalabas natin ang laki ng circuit at ang lalim ng two-qubit gate.
examples.suggested: Ipi-print natin ang laki ng circuit at ang two-qubit gate depth.
examples.why: "Inilalabas" (literally "we take out") is vague for printing output to the screen. "Ipi-print" is the usual word in technical Tagalog.

editor_note: The translation is faithful overall, and the key caveats hold: the Open Plan/session restriction in [27] and the COBYLA noise discussion in [51] are both intact. [20] gets the encoding direction backwards: "na ang ground state ay naka-encode sa optimal na solusyon" says the ground state is encoded in the solution, when the English says the ground state encodes the solution. The core link between the two still comes through, so it is not a FAIL. The other problems are calques and inconsistencies: "reduces to" in [38] is rendered as "bumababa sa" (numerically decreases), "incurs" in [27] as "magdurusa sa", "swamps" in [51] as "inaapakan", "na minimize" in [71] is missing its affix, and the heading in [37] is left fully in English while the other Step headings are translated.

examples.source: a cost Hamiltonian whose ground state encodes the optimal solution
examples.translation: isang cost Hamiltonian na ang ground state ay naka-encode sa optimal na solusyon
examples.suggested: isang cost Hamiltonian na ang ground state ay nag-e-encode ng optimal na solusyon
examples.why: 'naka-encode sa' means 'is encoded in', so the relationship runs backwards. The ground state should encode the solution, not the other way round.

examples.source: the cost Hamiltonian reduces to $H_C = ...$
examples.translation: ang cost Hamiltonian ay bumababa sa $H_C = ...$
examples.suggested: ang cost Hamiltonian ay nauuwi sa $H_C = ...$
examples.why: 'bumababa' means a value going down. Here 'reduces to' means 'simplifies to', so the literal rendering is a calque.

examples.source: each iteration incurs the full queue latency
examples.translation: ang bawat iteration ay magdurusa sa buong queue latency
examples.suggested: dadaan ang bawat iteration sa buong queue latency
examples.why: 'magdurusa' (to suffer) is a stiff, overly emotive calque of 'incurs'.

examples.source: Check that the cost minimized in the optimization loop has converged
examples.translation: Suriin na ang cost na minimize sa optimization loop ay nag-converge
examples.suggested: Suriin kung nag-converge na ang cost na na-minimize sa optimization loop
examples.why: The bare English verb 'minimize' is missing its Tagalog affix, and the word order is calqued.

examples.source: Step 1: Map classical inputs to a quantum problem
examples.translation: Step 1: Map classical inputs to a quantum problem
examples.suggested: Step 1: I-map ang mga classical input sa isang quantum problem
examples.why: This heading is left fully in English, while the Step 2, 3 and 4 headings ([44], [47], [55]) are translated.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The DD/MEM caveats in [43], [50] and [55], the 80%/10%/10% qubit-scoring weights in [36] and the 60-PUB same-job grouping in [47] all match the source. The problems are phrasing. [8] leaves "followed by measurement" untranslated in the middle of a Tagalog sentence, while [0] translates it as "na sinusundan ng measurement". [34] uses a stiff causative calque ("gumagawa sa inaasahang measured string na maging baligtad"). [50] renders "parallel" dictionary as "katulad na" ("similar"), which loses the sense that it is a companion record kept alongside the plotted one. [21] translates "For fun" literally as "Para sa kasiyahan".

examples.source: Build equivalent unitary and dynamic implementations of quantum Fourier transform followed by measurement (QFT+M).
examples.translation: Bumuo ng katumbas na unitary at dynamic implementations ng quantum Fourier transform followed by measurement (QFT+M).
examples.suggested: Bumuo ng katumbas na unitary at dynamic na implementasyon ng quantum Fourier transform na sinusundan ng measurement (QFT+M).
examples.why: An English clause is left in the middle of a Tagalog sentence, and [0] already translates the same phrase as 'na sinusundan ng measurement'.

examples.source: The classical-bit display order in Qiskit therefore makes the expected measured string the reverse of the zero-padded binary representation of $x$
examples.translation: Kaya naman, ang classical-bit display order sa Qiskit ay gumagawa sa inaasahang measured string na maging baligtad ng zero-padded binary representation ng $x$
examples.suggested: Kaya naman, dahil sa classical-bit display order ng Qiskit, ang inaasahang measured string ay ang baligtad ng zero-padded binary representation ng $x$
examples.why: This copies the English 'makes X the Y' causative structure and reads as machine translation.

examples.source: The parallel `raw_process_fidelity` dictionary retains an unmitigated calculation
examples.translation: Ang katulad na `raw_process_fidelity` dictionary ay pinananatili ang unmitigated na kalkulasyon
examples.suggested: Ang kasabay (hiwalay na) `raw_process_fidelity` dictionary ay nagtatabi ng unmitigated na kalkulasyon
examples.why: 'Katulad' means 'similar', but the source means a companion dictionary kept alongside the plotted one. The meaning shifts slightly but not in a way that misleads.

examples.source: For fun, make sure to compare these results to your results at the end
examples.translation: Para sa kasiyahan, siguraduhing ihambing ang mga resultang ito sa iyong mga resulta sa dulo
examples.suggested: Bilang dagdag na kasiyahan, ihambing mo ang mga resultang ito sa sarili mong resulta sa dulo
examples.why: This translates the English idiom word for word and sounds stiff.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. Nothing here would mislead a learner. The spin-up/right-half and spin-down/left-half mapping in [57], the initial_occupancies caveats in [60] and the accuracy discussion in [62] all match the English. A native editor would still fix a few things. The heading "Visualize the results" became "Mga resulta ng biswal" ("results of the visual"). [51] garbles "a gate set that the LUCJ ansatz naturally decomposes to" into "gate set na natural na na-decompose ang LUCJ ansatz", which has no clear subject or target. "Quantum chemistry" appears as both "Quantum na kimika" ([9], [20]) and "quantum chemistry" ([14], [24]). Smaller slips: "more efficient Dice" became "mas mahusay" ("better") in [71], "exact answer" became "tamang sagot" ("correct answer") in [62], and "Learning outcomes" was rendered as "Mga resulta ng pag-aaral", which reads like "study results".

examples.source: Visualize the results
examples.translation: Mga resulta ng biswal
examples.suggested: I-visualize ang mga resulta
examples.why: The translation reads as 'results of the visual'. It turns an instruction to plot the results into a garbled noun phrase.

examples.source: a gate set that the LUCJ ansatz naturally decomposes to
examples.translation: gate set na natural na na-decompose ang LUCJ ansatz
examples.suggested: gate set kung saan natural na nade-decompose ang LUCJ ansatz
examples.why: The relative clause has no linker. It reads as if the gate set is what decomposes the ansatz, so the relationship is unclear.

examples.source: the more efficient Dice software
examples.translation: ang mas mahusay na Dice software
examples.suggested: ang mas episyenteng Dice software
examples.why: 'Efficient' is a specific performance claim. 'Mahusay' means 'better' or 'skilled' in general, which makes the claim vaguer.

examples.source: Quantum chemistry and second quantization
examples.translation: Quantum na kimika at second quantization
examples.suggested: Quantum chemistry at second quantization
examples.why: Entries [14] and [24] keep 'quantum chemistry' in English, so the same field is named two ways in this file.

examples.source: within `1 mH` of the exact answer
examples.translation: nasa loob na tayo ng `1 mH` ng tamang sagot
examples.suggested: nasa loob na tayo ng `1 mH` ng eksaktong sagot
examples.why: 'Exact' refers to the exact-diagonalization reference value. 'Tamang' ('correct') loses that technical sense.

editor_note: All 11 rewritten headings are faithful, natural imperatives. For example, "Patakbuhin sa hardware gamit ang Fire Opal", "Tantiyahin ang mga single-qubit magnetization" and "Pagkukulay ng mga graph edge" all match their English, and "Step N" is kept the same way in every step heading.

The meaning is faithful throughout, including the ε-clipping caveat, the ~49% p=1 limit and the convergence-versus-sampling distinction, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Some things still need an edit. In [61] two intensifiers are dropped: "far fewer iterations" becomes plain "mas kaunting iteration" and "significantly better" becomes plain "mas mahusay". In [21] "reduces exactly to standard QAOA" is calqued as "eksaktong nababawas patungo sa", which reads as "is subtracted toward"; "nauuwi" would be better. The Step heading [43] is left entirely in English, and "Step 2/Step 4" appear in [42] and [56] even though the other headings use "Hakbang". There are also small grammar and fluency slips, such as "Nagbibigay ito ng COBYLA" in [55] and "kung gaano ito kontribuyente" in [40].

examples.source: converges quickly to near $-1.50$ (the exact optimum) with far fewer iterations ... it reaches a significantly better solution.
examples.translation: mabilis na nagko-converge sa malapit sa $-1.50$ ... gamit ang mas kaunting iteration ... umaabot ito sa mas mahusay na solusyon.
examples.suggested: ... gamit ang mas higit na kaunting iteration ... umaabot ito sa kapansin-pansing mas mahusay na solusyon.
examples.why: Dropped qualifiers 'far' and 'significantly' soften the key claim of the page. The direction is preserved, so this is minor.

examples.source: At $\varepsilon = 0.5$, WS-QAOA reduces exactly to standard QAOA.
examples.translation: Sa $\varepsilon = 0.5$, ang WS-QAOA ay eksaktong nababawas patungo sa standard QAOA.
examples.suggested: Sa $\varepsilon = 0.5$, eksaktong nauuwi ang WS-QAOA sa standard QAOA.
examples.why: 'nababawas' means 'is subtracted/decreased'. It is a literal calque of 'reduces' and does not carry the sense of 'reduces to / becomes'.

examples.source: Step 2: Optimize problem for quantum hardware execution
examples.translation: Step 2: Optimize problem for quantum hardware execution
examples.suggested: Hakbang 2: I-optimize ang problema para sa quantum hardware execution
examples.why: This heading was left untranslated, while Steps 1, 3 and 4 use 'Hakbang'. Entries [42] and [56] also say 'Step'.

examples.source: This gives COBYLA a strong starting signal aligned with the classical solution.
examples.translation: Nagbibigay ito ng COBYLA ng malakas na starting signal na naaayon sa classical solution.
examples.suggested: Nagbibigay ito sa COBYLA ng malakas na starting signal na naaayon sa classical solution.
examples.why: The recipient needs the marker 'sa'. 'ng COBYLA' reads as if COBYLA is being given.

editor_note: Four of the five rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally: "Paggamit ng oras ng QPU: 11s", "Mga Quantum Circuit", "Nilikha ni:" and the copyright notice, which keeps "derivative work" in English as a legal term and keeps the requirement to mark modified files. Entry 109 has one problem. The heading "Post-process" became "Pagpoproseso", which means just "Processing". It drops the "post-" (after execution) meaning that marks this as the step where results are processed. That is a lost qualifier, not a false claim, so it counts as a minor issue.

examples.source: Post-process {#post-process}
examples.translation: Pagpoproseso {#post-process}
examples.suggested: Post-processing {#post-process}  (or: Pagproseso ng mga resulta {#post-process})
examples.why: 'Pagpoproseso' means generic 'processing' and loses the 'post-' meaning. In the Qiskit patterns workflow this step specifically means processing the results after the job runs.

editor_note: Entry 6 is faithful: "Isang scalable na physical system na may mahusay na nailalarawang mga qubit" keeps both qualifiers, with "mahusay na nailalarawan" for "well-characterized". This matches the page's quoted English criterion in entry 14.
